title: Emit metrics + tracing for Private backup/restore operations (with error categorization)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Private deployments: backup/restore workflows now emit structured Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry spans, including failure categorization to power dashboards/alerts and restore drill reporting.
description: Motivation: SRE/on-call and customers need a consistent way to answer “are backups running?” and “why did the last restore drill fail?” across VPC + on-prem Private installs. We already log backup/restore steps in the installer, but logs alone are hard to alert on and don’t support reliable aggregation. This PR adds: (1) structured Prometheus metrics for backup + restore operations (success/failure, duration, bytes, last success timestamps), (2) OpenTelemetry tracing spans with consistent attributes for per-step visibility, and (3) explicit error categorization to drive dashboards/alerts and reduce pager noise. Scope: This instruments the control-plane backup/restore path (installer-driven + control-plane endpoints) and adds common helpers used by both “backup create” and “restore apply”. It does not change backup artifact format or encryption behavior. Metrics (Prometheus): - redwood_private_backup_runs_total{result,storage_backend,component,format_version} (counter) - redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds_bucket{result,storage_backend,component} (histogram) - redwood_private_backup_bytes_total{result,storage_backend,component} (counter) - redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{storage_backend,component,format_version} (gauge) - redwood_private_restore_runs_total{result,source_backend,target_env,format_version} (counter) - redwood_private_restore_duration_seconds_bucket{result,step} (histogram) - redwood_private_restore_validation_failures_total{check_name,error_category} (counter) - redwood_private_backup_restore_errors_total{operation,step,error_category} (counter; emitted on failure paths only) Tracing (OTel): Adds a top-level span per operation: “private.backup.create” and “private.restore.apply”, with child spans for steps: preflight, quiesce, snapshot, encrypt, upload, verify, bootstrap, migrate, validate. Spans include attributes: deployment_id, cluster_id (if known), namespace, storage_backend, artifact_manifest_version, backup_id/restore_id, step, result, error_category. Error categorization: Introduces a shared enum + mapping helper that classifies common failure types in a stable way for alerting/reporting. Categories include: preflight_failed, quiesce_failed, snapshot_failed, encrypt_failed, upload_failed, download_failed, verify_failed, bootstrap_failed, migrate_failed, validation_failed, compatibility_failed, permission_denied, kms_unavailable, timeout, rate_limited, unknown. Mapping is conservative: if we can’t confidently classify, we emit unknown and preserve the raw error message in logs/traces (not as a metric label) to avoid high-cardinality explosions. RBAC / permissions: No new privileges are required for the control plane, but installer pods/jobs must be allowed to emit metrics to the existing collector in Private installs. This PR reuses existing OTEL exporter wiring and the in-cluster Prometheus scrape config. Testing: - Unit tests for error classification mapping and label sanitization - Integration test in staging that runs a forced failure (bad bucket creds) and asserts metrics increments + spans have error_category - Manual validation: ran backup create / restore apply in dev VPC env; verified dashboard panels populate (see follow-up in observability-pack PR). Notes on cardinality: - No metric labels include backup_id, restore_id, customer name, or raw error strings - deployment_id is included only as a tracing attribute (not a metric label) - component label is constrained to a small set (control_plane_db, control_plane_config, k8s_manifests, audit_logs_export) - step label is constrained to known step names and used only on histogram for restore duration per step (bounded) Follow-ups: - Alert rules + dashboards land in observability-pack (PR-94) - SLO definitions tracked in slo-toolkit (PR-67) - Backup status endpoint is in PR-24318 (separate) which will consume these metrics for UI surfacing

conversation: Allison Grant (review): Please avoid high-cardinality labels. Specifically: do not include deployment_id as a metric label, and ensure step/component are bounded enums. Also add a short note in-code about why we don’t attach raw error strings to metrics.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated. deployment_id is trace-only now; component + step are constants with a compile-time list; raw error strings remain logs/traces only. Added comments + a label sanitizer that rejects unknown values.

Sean Gallagher (review): Can we add a metric to support paging on “no backups in X hours” without querying counters? A last_success gauge would help. Also, can restore validation failures be separated from “restore failed to run” so we can alert differently?

Sergio Costa (author): Added redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds (gauge) emitted only on successful completion. Added restore_validation_failures_total with check_name + error_category to separate validation outcomes from workflow failures.

Ethan Park (review): Error categorization: please ensure compatibility failures (format version mismatch) are separate from generic verify_failed, and that it’s deterministic across versions. Also prefer stable names (snake_case) since SRE will write alert rules against them.
Sergio Costa (author): Added compatibility_failed and mapped version mismatch/manifest parse issues there. Enum names are snake_case and tested for stability.

Marcus Lin (review): Confirm we’re not leaking sensitive info via attributes/labels. Traces may include deployment_id; ensure that’s not customer-identifying beyond our internal UUID. Also avoid putting bucket names or KMS key IDs on spans.
Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed. No bucket names, no KMS key IDs. deployment_id is an internal UUID and only in traces. Added a denylist in attribute builder for common URL/bucket patterns.
Neha Kapoor (approval): Looks good. The last_success gauge + error_category should unblock alerting. Please make sure histogram buckets are reasonable; overly fine buckets can be noisy.
Sergio Costa (author): Buckets set to [1, 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1200, 1800] seconds for operation-level and tighter for step-level. Happy to tune post-merge based on staging data.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved with the label/cardinality changes.
